Summary: The sources indicate that agentic AI systems consume substantially more energy per interaction than single-turn inference, with a 280-fold decline in inference costs since 2022 driving a rebound effect where cheaper inference enables more agentic deployments, each consuming more energy per user goal than single-shot queries. For example, System A reports 50 J per inference but requires four attempts before delivering a correct answer, accumulating 200 J per successful goal, while System B succeeds in one attempt at 70 J per goal. The energy per successful goal (EpG) aggregates total workflow energy across all execution attempts, including failures and retries, normalized by successfully completed goals. Agentic AI workloads, where a single user goal triggers multi-step orchestration, tool calls, retries, and failure recovery, are being targeted for edge deployment, with substantial energy costs driven by orchestration structure and CPU-side processing.
